headline: Trump tries to fire a Fed governor

beats.text: On August twentieth, Trump's handpicked housing regulator accused Fed Governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud. No charges. No indictment. Just a post.

beats.caption: You going to fire Lisa Cook, the Fed governor, over her mortgage? / I don't know if she doesn't resign.
beats.label: via CNBC

beats.text: Three days later he sent her a termination letter anyway. Problem: Fed governors serve fourteen-year terms and can't be fired by a Truth Social post.

beats.caption: So, I'll fire her if she doesn't resign.
beats.label: via CNBC

beats.text: Cook wasn't having it — she hired a lawyer to fight the letter instead.

beats.caption: I will not resign. I will continue to carry out my duties.
beats.label: via NewsNation

beats.text: Under the Federal Reserve Act, a governor can only be fired for actual cause — proven, not just declared in a letter.

beats.caption: The president doesn't have the authority to sack her.
beats.label: via FRANCE 24

beats.text: Cook sued. The fight over who runs the Fed outlasted the entire month.
